**Correction to my triage comment above — reason 3 was wrong.**

I wrote that `**Blocked-by: #14381.**` "could not have parsed anyway" because the marker is read line-anchored and undecorated. That is not how the gate reads it.

`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs:113-117` says the opposite, deliberately:

> The line may be DECORATED in either channel — 「`Blocked-by: #9612`」 is the natural markdown for a line meant to be grepped, and reading it as absent left #10063 permanently blocked in silence (#10102).

So decoration is tolerated on purpose, and my reason 3 was the exact mistake #10102 exists to prevent. Withdrawn.

The other two reasons stand and are what removed the line:

1. it pointed at a **PR**, not an issue — and PR #14381 has no issue lifecycle for the unlock sweep to read;
2. it was **exhausted** — #14381 merged at 2026-09-02T05:28:42Z.

The grading is unchanged: `pm:queue`, ready now, scope as ruled above.

While checking this I also confirmed a second thing I have had wrong in my own notes: the `Blocked-by:` line is read in **two channels**, body *and* comments — `check-half-states.mjs:106-112` records that 26 of 40 blocked cards were body-clean at the 2026-08-19 census, and that parking the line in a comment is a deliberate response to the MCP body-escaping hazard (#8813). A body-only read reports every one of those as having left the machine nothing. Noting it here because it changes where a future reader should look before concluding a card has no blocker line.

⭐ **Two probes moving in opposite directions against live controls is the strongest form of this reading** — a vacuous probe cannot produce both. That matters here because the 0-vs-0 trap cost this lane a wrong landing note on #14406 earlier in the shift.

### What this actually fixes, in business terms

`content/docs/ui/translations.mdx:248` carried, under the heading **"Honest limits worth knowing before you plan around them"** — the section customers read *specifically to plan around* — the sentence *"Validation messages are not translated through bundles."* That has been **false since 17.3.0**: `objectValidationMessageKey` (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`) is read on the write path by the rule evaluator (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`, six call sites through `authoredRuleMessage`).

So a shipped, paid-for localization capability was denied by our own documentation:

- a customer running a multi-language tenant either ships English validation errors to non-English users, or builds a workaround (locale logic inside rule expressions, or duplicated rules per locale) that the platform then has to support;
- ⭐ and an **AI agent authoring a metadata app reads that same page as its context** — so it would never emit the `_validations` key, and had no route to discover the capability, because the doc explicitly denied it existed. On the anti-AI-error axis that is worse than a missing guardrail: the documentation was actively teaching the error.

The ADR amendment is the other half, and it is insurance rather than paperwork: without it, a later correctness pass reading the 17.0.0 retirement of the top-level `validationMessages` group (#4667) would conclude that validation-message translation was killed **as policy**, and would either refuse to re-add it or delete the new object-scoped key as a violation. ⛔ The two are not the same route — the retired one was keyed by rule name alone and could not tell two objects' rules apart; the live one is object-scoped and shipped with its reader.

### ⚠️ Still open on the same page — this was one of three

- **#15435** — the same "What you can translate" table still omits the **`bulkActions`** and **`datasets`** groups, both shipped and live.
- **#15437** — the ADR-0087 conversion text still stops at the authored literal and never names the object-scoped key, so the prescription an author sees on writing the retired key is itself a dead end.

⇒ The systemic reading, offered for triage and ⛔ not as a ruling: this page misstates or omits **three** shipped translation surfaces, and #15438 fixed one. The defect class is **discoverability of shipped capability**, not three unrelated p3 doc nits.
